items.label: Neural Strain persists across days; sleep and night patches only partially restore it

items.intent: Strain does not reset when a new day opens. Whatever a day closes at is what tomorrow starts at, minus what sleep or a night patch buys back, so a bad day compounds unless spent down.
items.tier: 2, a rule needed once at the moment it starts mattering, not a recurring number: the regen figure itself (+10 from sleep) is already tier 0/1, always visible on NIGHT.SYS's own strain block, so a tip would be redundant. Not tier 0: the fact that strain does NOT reset is a negative claim no label currently makes, and the one place it is stated in flavor text (a Tuesday morning line) cannot appear before day 9 by its own cycling logic, verified against content/story.ts's morningLine().
items.engineNote: Needs a new TeachWhen union member 'strainShort' in content/teaching.ts, firing on day.strain < 100 when NightContent first mounts. Signal is a one-line read at the call site (windows/night.tsx); no reducer change. Also needs a new anchor class kp-teach-strain (existing kp-teach-<anchor> system, not new UI) positioned near NIGHT.SYS's strain block, distinct from night-shop's existing 'patch' anchor.

items.spec: In DIVE.EXE's result overlay (components/game/duel.tsx, the dv-result-bill block), the row currently gated only on `state.phase !== "won"` renders 'NEURAL STRAIN' / 'ZEROED. THE RUN IS OVER.' on every loss, including an ordinary ticket loss where day.strain is untouched and the shop day continues normally (day-reducer.ts's duelFinished handler bills no strain on a loss, by design: 'the loss already costs the ticket'). This contradicts the room's own LossToast, which correctly reads 'CORE LOST. NO CHARGE, NO STRAIN.' for the identical event. Fix: distinguish an ordinary ticket loss from a genuine bust (day.strain actually at or heading to zero) and give the ordinary case its own accurate row, matching LossToast's wording (no charge, no strain billed, the ticket goes home unfinished). Reserve 'THE RUN IS OVER' framing only for a state where that is literally true.
acceptance: Losing an ordinary ticket dive (day.ticket was set, the loss is not a strain-zero bust) never renders the words 'ZEROED' or 'THE RUN IS OVER' anywhere in the result overlay.
The ordinary-loss case's strain row states the true outcome: no strain billed, wording consistent with LossToast's 'CORE LOST. NO CHARGE, NO STRAIN.'

If any duel outcome can still cause a genuine same-instant bust, that case keeps an accurate 'the day is over' statement; if no such case currently exists in the day-as-run design, the unconditional row is simply removed rather than left reachable through dead logic.
